subject: MedNova DPA: LLM use exclusion and output custody
messages:
From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@mednova.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: MedNova Procurement <procurement@mednova.com>, Jones & Reed <j.reed@jonesreed.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: LLM DPA asks: training exclusion + prompt/response custody

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — MedNova is excited about the latency and observability features. Before we proceed to procurement, legal needs to confirm a couple of things for the DPA and SOW:

- We require an explicit "no-training / no-model-improvement" commitment for MedNova tenant data (including prompts & responses).
- Prompt/response outputs generated by the service must be licensed to MedNova (we need clarity on derivative/IP language).
- We need a list of subprocessors that will touch tenant data during inference and any plans for cross-border transfers or KMS access by third parties.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: (1) commit in the DPA to no-training on our data, (2) provide customer-retained output licensing language, and (3) provide the current subprocessors list and onshore/offshore KMS options?

I attached an initial list of redlines from our GC for context. If this makes sense, we can schedule a quick call next week with procurement and legal.

Thanks,
Sarah Connors
Senior Counsel, Data Privacy
MedNova Health
Attachment: MedNova_DPA_Redline.docx (docx)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@mednova.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LLM DPA asks: training exclusion + prompt/response custody

Sarah — appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front: yes (we can commit to no-training for tenant data when requested and operationalize it), yes (we can provide customer-favorable output licensing language), and yes on a subprocessors list + KMS residency options.

Operational notes / what we'll need from you:
- Confirmation of the exact scope: is the ask "no-training on all tenant inputs + outputs" or "no-training on anything marked with an opt-out flag" (we support both).
- Residency preference (US-only KMS/onshore processing) and whether ephemeral KV/session caching is acceptable if pinned to onshore nodes.
- Procurement timeline and whether DocuSign + a short tech addendum is sufficient.

I've attached our proposed DPA addendum (redwood-data-processing-addendum_v2.pdf) and looped in Kimberly (legal) and Marissa (ops) to provide language and an implementation checklist. Happy to set a 30-min call to go through the redline.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales Director
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-data-processing-addendum_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@mednova.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed clause text + operational checklist (no-training + output license)

Hi Sarah,

Thanks for the note — appreciate the precision. Below is proposed DPA language we can offer; I included brief operational points after the legal text. Happy to iterate with Jones & Reed.

Proposed DPA clause (illustrative):
"No-Model-Training Commitment. Redwood agrees that it will not use Transmitted Data (as defined in the DPA) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise update model weights or parameters of any model used in Redwood's inference platform, whether directly or through third parties, except: (i) as required to comply with lawful requests; (ii) for aggregated and irreversibly anonymized telemetry used solely for platform stability (no content-level retention); or (iii) where Customer provides explicit, documented, and revocable consent. For clarity, "Transmitted Data" includes prompts, conversational history, and generated outputs unless Customer elects otherwise in writing."

Proposed output licensing addendum:
"Output License. Customer is granted an exclusive (to the extent legally possible), perpetual, worldwide right to use, reproduce, and sublicense Outputs generated from Customer Transmitted Data. Redwood shall not assert ownership over Outputs or derivatives thereof, and shall not use Outputs to improve models or services absent Customer's express opt-in."

Operational checklist (high level):
- Implement an opt-out flag at request header level (x-redwood-no-train: true) and tenant-level account setting.
- Route flagged requests to "no-train" serving pool with strict KV cache eviction policies; ensure no persistent write-back to training pipelines.
- Provide subprocessors list (current) and a change-notice window of 30 days for MedNova review.
- Provide KMS residency options: (a) Redwood-managed US KMS, (b) customer-managed KMS in customer's cloud via integration, (c) on-prem HSM option via Private deployment.
- Deliver evidence bundle on request: operational runbook, audit logs around model-training pipelines, and ephemeral caching screenshots/logs.

Attachment: redwood-no-train-ops-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

If that aligns with MedNova's requirements, we can prepare a tracked-change DPA and a short SOC-like evidence pack for procurement. Let me know if Jones & Reed would like different wording on exclusivity (we can scope to "Outputs" vs. "Derivatives").

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Associate General Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

P.S. Marissa — can your team confirm estimated timeline to stand up the no-train serving pool and evidence pack?

From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@mednova.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jones & Reed <j.reed@jonesreed.com>, MedNova Procurement <procurement@mednova.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 11:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed clause text + operational checklist (no-training + output license)

Kimberly — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we need. A few clarifying points from MedNova legal and procurement after initial review with our counsel:

1) Scope: We need the "No-Model-Training Commitment" to cover all inputs and outputs unless we explicitly opt-in for a specific pilot. So default = no-training.
2) Exclusivity: Our counsel prefers explicit language that Redwood "shall not assert property or IP rights in Outputs" and that Redwood will not use Outputs to improve models even in aggregated form without opt-in.
3) Subprocessors: We need the current list and an assurance that any new subprocessor will be subject to a confidentiality + no-train obligation prior to handling MedNova data.

We've attached our annotated redline; the team would like a 30-min alignment call next Tue (5/19) at 10am PT if that works for your side. In terms of evidence, procurement will want the subprocessors list, KMS residency confirmation, and a simple statement of how ephemeral caching is isolated from training pipelines.

Thanks — we'll wait for your confirmation on the call and any updated tracked DPA text.

Sarah
Senior Counsel, Data Privacy
MedNova Health
Attachment: MedNova_DPA_Redline.docx (docx)
